newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 30.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Wednesday and main factors likely to affect trading.
* Shares are likely to persist in their downtrend prompted by poor first quarter results of major companies, All Asia Securities research head Helen Alvarez said.
* The Dow's overnight rise is unlikely to lift the local equities market as PLDT's ADR in New York was sharply down by $1 5/8 tp $56 5/8, traders said.
* San Miguel Corp said it earned a net income of 1.11 billion pesos for the first quarter of the year compared with 781 million pesos last year.
* The Manila Electric Co reported an 8.3 percent increase in first quarter net at 1.10 billion pesos but its kilowatt-hour (kwh) sales grew only 5.4 percent to 4.2 billion kwhs.
* The Philippine Central Bank set a 20 percent limit on loan exposure of banks to the real estate sector.
* Alaska Milk Corp posted a 63 million net income for the first three months of the year from nine million the same period in 1996.

* Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co said its net income in the first three months reached 1.25 billion pesos compared to 1.0 billion a year ago. It decided to book reserves of 500 million pesos in the interest of prudent banking.
* On Tuesday, the main stock market index plunged to its lowest level in two years closing loqwe by 128.87 points at 2,708.44.
* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones rose 179.01 points to 6,962.03.
* The peso closed lower at 26.370 to the dollar vs 26.367
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.28125 percent.
